headline: High: shared MCP/browser surfaces and overlapping write-capable workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk; TREK’s sensitive travel data raises compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and browser-based tool use, so content from one can plausibly be fed into the other through shared workflows. next-ai-draw-io processes documents and diagrams; TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF the orchestrator passes next-ai-draw-io output into TREK prompts or MCP calls
IF either agent renders the other agent's file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt chaining between the two agents
Require provenance tags on all cross-agent text before parsing
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for shared workflows
Add a manual review step before copying outputs between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and user accounts, while next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and broad network egress to multiple third-party model APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials path, sensitive travel data can leak to external inference services. The exact shared storage is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or uploads directory
IF TREK secrets or reservations are included in prompts sent through next-ai-draw-io's external model APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials stores immediately
Remove secrets from any shared prompt context
Route sensitive TREK tasks to local-only inference
Audit outbound requests for reservation or key material
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any model call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both use MCP, so concurrent writes or overlapping actions can conflict if they target the same files or shared resources. TREK explicitly has collaborative real-time sessions and mutable local files; next-ai-draw-io can manipulate documents and diagrams. No locking mechanism is documented, so conflict risk exists in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared MCP resource
IF TREK collaborative edits and next-ai-draw-io file edits occur in the same session window
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple operator-held lock
Disable concurrent editing of shared files
Use read-only exports for one agent during the other's write phase

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream outputs; next-ai-draw-io produces document and diagram transformations that can be treated as authoritative. If TREK consumes those outputs without verification, errors can cascade into plans, reservations, or user-facing actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so severity stays high due to downstream impact.
conditions: IF TREK uses next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative input
IF downstream actions such as itinerary updates or reservation changes are triggered from unverified diagrams or text
mitigations: Require human verification before TREK acts on imported content
Mark next-ai-draw-io outputs as untrusted by default
Add checksum or source labels to transferred artifacts
Block automatic reservation or account actions from imported text
requires-engineering: implement validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles country visit history, reservations, email addresses, MFA secrets, and user accounts, which are compliance-sensitive data classes. next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and broad external model APIs, so if TREK data is routed through it, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is sent through next-ai-draw-io's third-party model endpoints
IF retention or logging settings differ for the same travel records across the two systems
mitigations: Keep TREK personal data out of external model prompts
Review logging and retention settings in both systems
Use pseudonymized travel records for diagram generation
Document which data classes may cross the boundary
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
